# `barcode` commands

## `barcode generate`

Give items without a code an EAN-13 barcode in the restricted-circulation range (prefix 2, for the company's own labels), numbered from the company counter with its check digit. Existing codes never change: a named item that has one is skipped and listed. Each change is an item update in the item's history. `--dry-run` shows the codes it would assign.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/barcode.generate` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow barcode generate --items '["Brass Shutoff Valve","Copper Coupling"]' --reason "Label the parts shelf" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "barcode generate", "input": {"items": ["Brass Shutoff Valve", "Copper Coupling"]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `--items` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Items to number: ID, full name or barcode each. Omitted: every active inventory part, assembly and non-inventory part with no code. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |

| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/barcode.generate`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assigned` | array[object] | yes | no | — | Each item given a code, with its new EAN-13. |
| `assigned[].item_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `assigned[].item` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `assigned[].barcode` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `skipped` | array[object] | yes | no | — | Named items left as they are: one that has a code keeps it. |
| `skipped[].item_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `skipped[].item` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `skipped[].barcode` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `skipped[].reason` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `next_number` | integer | yes | no | — | The company counter after this run: the next code's serial number. |

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "assigned": [],
  "next_number": 1,
  "skipped": []
}
```

## `barcode lookup`

Say what a scanned or typed code names: the item carrying it as its barcode, its on-hand quantity by site and the line fields to use (pass the code itself as `item` on any document line; it resolves after id and name). A code on two active items (a duplicate kept from before codes were checked) is ambiguous and both are listed. An unknown code is not an error: the answer says so and how to assign it to an item.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/barcode.lookup` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow barcode lookup --code 0012345678905 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "barcode lookup", "input": {"code": "0012345678905"}, "company": "Company ID or name"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | `--code` | string | yes | no | — | The code as scanned or typed, e.g. `0012345678905`.; minimum length 1; maximum length 128 |
| `as_of` | `--as-of` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Date the on-hand figures are read as of (ISO). Defaults to today. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/barcode.lookup`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `as_of` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `found` | boolean | yes | no | — | True when the code names exactly one record (preferring active ones). |
| `kind` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | `item`, `ambiguous` when it names more than one, or null when nothing carries it. |
| `match` | object \| null | yes | yes | — | The one record the code names; null when none or ambiguous. |
| `match.kind` | string | yes | no | — | What the code names: `item` (bins, serial numbers and lots join as they gain codes). |
| `match.id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `match.name` | string | yes | no | — | The record's full name. |
| `match.type` | string | yes | no | — | The item type. |
| `match.active` | boolean | yes | no | — | — |
| `match.barcode` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `match.on_hand` | array[object] | yes | no | — | Quantity on hand by site as of as_of; sites holding none are left out. |
| `match.on_hand[].site_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `match.on_hand[].site` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `match.on_hand[].quantity` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `match.line_fields` | object[string, string] | yes | no | — | Fields to put on a document line for this code, e.g. {"item": "Copper Coupling"}. |
| `matches` | array[object] | yes | no | — | Every record carrying the code, active first: two when a duplicate is kept. |
| `matches[].kind` | string | yes | no | — | What the code names: `item` (bins, serial numbers and lots join as they gain codes). |
| `matches[].id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `matches[].name` | string | yes | no | — | The record's full name. |
| `matches[].type` | string | yes | no | — | The item type. |
| `matches[].active` | boolean | yes | no | — | — |
| `matches[].barcode` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `matches[].on_hand` | array[object] | yes | no | — | Quantity on hand by site as of as_of; sites holding none are left out. |
| `matches[].on_hand[].site_id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `matches[].on_hand[].site` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `matches[].on_hand[].quantity` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `matches[].line_fields` | object[string, string] | yes | no | — | Fields to put on a document line for this code, e.g. {"item": "Copper Coupling"}. |
| `ambiguous` | boolean | yes | no | — | — |
| `valid_ean13` | boolean | yes | no | — | Whether the code is a 13-digit EAN with a correct check digit (other symbologies are still looked up). |
| `message` | string | yes | no | — | The answer in words; for an unknown code, how to assign it to an item. |

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "ambiguous": false,
  "as_of": "value",
  "code": "SI-1",
  "found": false,
  "kind": null,
  "match": null,
  "matches": [],
  "message": "value",
  "valid_ean13": false
}
```
